title: The silhouette had nowhere to sit: the enemy chassis was darker than the ground it stood on, and nothing in the repo could say so

verified.THE DEFECT, measured off the previous bu: median deltaL 0.0922, worst 0.0751, 0 of 11 clearing 0.25, on a frame that also carries film grain at +/-0.03. The darkest pixel of every creature was already 0.008 against ground at 0.09 — there was no room left DOWNWARD, which is why the previous pass's answer (MIN_AGENT_PX 17 -> 24, size not contrast) could not have worked

open: INTEGRATOR: bump LcnArtCache.ART_VERSION (game/view/render/art_cache.gd, currently v19). `_hide()` changed and two new mask keys were added, so every cached agent_*.png on a dev box is stale art — the frame lab's own header names this exact trap ('the keener was redrawn and re-measured at an identical 117 screen pixels because v17/agent_keener.png already existed'). I am not allowed to edit that file. I deleted user://art_cache/v19 on this box; any machine that still has it renders the old chassis.

INTEGRATOR: tests/render/night_contrast.tscn is a standalone .tscn, and tools/check.sh runs standalone suites HEADLESS — so it prints UNCHECKED / TESTS PASSED, PARTIAL and check.sh records it as a SKIP that downgrades the verdict to PARTIAL. Exactly what tests/render/frame_lab.tscn does today. It only asks its question under xvfb: `xvfb-run -a -s "-screen 0 1920x1080x24" $GODOT --path . --resolution 1920x1080 tests/render/night_contrast.tscn`. check.sh is not mine to change.

PERF NOT MEASURED — do not read anything into this. tests/render/render_perf.tscn reported `FAIL collect 4222 us over budget 3000 us` while the frame lab and the reachability probe were also running on the same four cores; D1.json's reference for that stage is 2133-2155 us. render_perf stresses 1700 BUILDINGS and stages no agents at all, and I did not touch _collect, so my change cannot reach that stage — but only the integrator, on a quiet box, can say that with a number.

tests/render/night_contrast.tscn PRINTED ONE FALSE GREEN before it was believed, and the lesson generalises. Against the parent commit `_judge` raised on its first row (`ground_luma` does not exist there); a raised GDScript call abandons the WHOLE function; `rows` stayed empty, nothing reached the failure list, both hours 'completed', and the run printed TESTS PASSED over a build whose night is measurably blank. The `rows.size() < MIN_FOUND` guard did not save it because that guard is also inside `_judge`. The graded count is now recorded as the LAST statement of `_judge` and the verdict is computed from outside it. ANY suite in this repo that computes its verdict inside the function that can abort has the same hole.

I WROTE A WRONG DIAGNOSIS INTO A COMMIT MESSAGE AND CORRECTED IT IN THE NEXT ONE. I read artifacts/P13/frames/crowd.png at thumbnail size, called its pale figures white cut-out citizens, and committed that as fact. Differencing the frame against its own control plate — which was sitting beside it — puts every agent where it should be, dark on bright snow with boot prints behind it. The pale shapes are TURRETS, lit and snow-capped, barrels out. The arithmetic defect was real but lived at DUSK, and only adding dusk as a third graded hour found it (45-79% of every figure reading as lit, deltaL 0.60 against a design target of 0.38). Commit 756bfff carries the correction.

AND THE GATE I FIRST WROTE FOR DUSK WAS WRONG TOO: an 'is this figure lit' fraction, which fired on 17 of 18 figures on the CORRECTED build. Looking at wave_dusk.png settled it — at dusk the treatment is deliberately half on and the figures are legitimately lit. What is wrong at 0.60 is the SIZE of the separation, so the gate is now a ceiling. Every other bar in that suite is a floor, and a treatment that over-drives clears all of them.

[P14]/[P15]: the wave now carries a cold rim and the city's people a warm one, so friend and foe separate by HUE as well as by value. If either part tints agents, that separation is the thing to preserve.

NEXT PASS ON THIS, a look note rather than a defect: at deep night the eleven read as one cold faction because the body lift is a single hue (FOE_BODY). The hot cores each was drawn with survive — LcnSpriteFactory._extract_fill deliberately spares anything over 0.32 luminance — but the chassis no longer carries per-kind colour after dark. Per-kind RIM hues would give the roster identity at range without spending any of the contrast budget.

The blob bar in night_contrast is MIN_FOUND 15 of 18 and the measurement is 17. The one that never makes it is the frost shade, drawn as a luminous translucent hood that fades to nothing at the hem, so its solid area is genuinely small: it clears the contrast bar (deltaL 0.36-0.42) and misses the 60 px blob. Either the creature wants more body or the bar wants to be per-silhouette-area. I left the bar honest rather than tuned to the answer.

Not graded: the strategic zoom (0.24). night_contrast photographs 0.60 only, because that is where the legends say the camera sits and where the brief aimed. MIN_RIM_PX drops the contour under 9 screen pixels and the body lift has no zoom gate, so the treatment survives down there in principle — nobody has photographed a wave at 0.24 and said so.
